name: Street Custom 'Prophet' Laser Pointer Weapon
description: A high-powered laser weapon disguised as — or built from — industrial laser cutting modules stacked in series within a tube roughly the size of a flashlight. The Prophet concentrates coherent light into a beam capable of causing instant retinal destruction at distance and thermal burns on skin with sustained exposure. The build uses commercially available laser diodes intended for industrial cutting applications, wired in parallel to achieve dangerous power levels. The weapon is favored by street-level operators for its concealability, silence, and the terrifying precision of a weapon that can blind someone from across a room before they know they are being targeted.
specifications:
beam type: Visible coherent light, 450nm wavelength
power output: 5-20W depending on diode count
effective range: Line of sight, lethal to eyes at 500+ meters
thermal effect: Second-degree burns at 5 meters with 3-second exposure
weight: 0.3-0.8 kg
power source: Lithium cell pack, 2-5 minutes continuous
concealability: Flashlight or pen-sized form factor
story_hooks: A sniper-style blinding campaign has left fourteen people permanently blind in a Tier 2 commercial district — the attacks are precise, targeted, and the weapon leaves no ballistic evidence.
A batch of Prophet builds is circulating that use an unstable diode configuration prone to thermal runaway — the weapons are blinding their users as often as their targets.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately mundane cylinder disguised as an industrial flashlight or inspection tool. The form factor is deliberately unremarkable—something a maintenance worker or corpo field tech might carry without a second glance. The tube tapers slightly toward the front, where an unassuming optical lens sits flush with the casing. No obvious barrel, no aggressive angles. Deceptively compact and ordinary.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light in hand despite the serial-stacked diode architecture inside—feels like a quality flashlight, slightly forward-weighted due to the energy cell pack positioned near the grip. Balanced for single-handed operation. The weight distribution suggests industrial intent rather than weapon design.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum tube body housing the diode stack; polycarbonate or acrylic lens housing at the front; custom-fab internal copper heat-sink matrix for thermal dissipation from parallel-wired laser diodes
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray or black anodized aluminum with brushed texture to reduce reflectivity. The optical lens is recessed behind a protective collar of darker polymer. Wear patterns consistent with field use—scuff marks, minor oxidation, handling marks on the grip section.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte gunmetal gray or industrial black | Accents: copper-colored heat venting ports along the tube body; faint blue glow visible inside the lens housing when powered (450nm coherent light bleeding slightly through the optics)
physical_description.grip_texture: Knurled aluminum or grip-tape wrapped handle section—textured for assured single-handed control even if hands are wet or gloved. Tactile enough to feel like legitimate tool hardware.
distinctive_features: Flush optical lens recessed 2-3mm behind protective aluminum collar
Three micro heat-venting ports along the mid-tube, angled to disperse thermal bloom
Concealed power indicator: tiny LED (red/green) at the rear grip that only glows if powered and in standby
Modular lens cap that screws on to complete the 'flashlight' aesthetic
Serial stacking visible in shadow inside the tube mouth—multiple diode modules visible as faint circular elements
Grip activation: pressure-sensor pad integrated into the textured grip (no trigger mechanism)
Faint radiator fins molded into the internal heat-sink structure, visible through transparent sections of the tube
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom's Φ symbol (stylized phi) stamped subtly into the aluminum just below the optical lens, barely visible unless lit from specific angles. No brand name, no model designation—only a laser-etched serial code on the bottom grip collar. Unmarked beyond intentional anonymity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but field-worn. The anodized finish shows minor handling scuffs and micro-abrasions consistent with daily carry in pocket or kit bag. Heat vents accumulate dust and micro-debris. The optical lens is kept clean—essential to function—but the protective collar shows weathering. No active rust, but the patina suggests age and street-level use rather than corpo-grade upkeep.
